metadata.case_name: Velvet Divorce: Czech Republic vs Slovakia
metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: The framework's flagship near-controlled experiment: holding event type constant (multinational federation dissolution, same years, same end-of-communism trigger), high P1 should predict a peaceful 'Velvet Divorce' -- the explicit contrast with Yugoslavia (lower P1 -> war).
metadata.notes: Czechoslovakia dissolved into 2 successor states via negotiated peaceful breakup (natural/manageable range, gated by high P1). Pre-event 1996. These countries are NOT in the user M-score dataset; post-event trajectory is qualitative. 1996 pillar values are ordinal estimates. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

pre_event.event_description: Velvet Divorce: peaceful 1993 dissolution of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia; divergent (both successful) post-divorce trajectories.

context.growth_trajectory: rising / converges upward to EU core

Czech Republic.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 high, balanced -> MI relatively high, narrow spread; well above Yugoslav/post-Soviet floors. WGI Rule of Law high (upper tier of post-communist); Govt Effectiveness high; Regulatory Quality high (Klaus reforms). HDI 1995 high band; GDP per cap PPP 1996 higher than Slovakia; political stability high. Ordering: Czech >= Slovakia. Pillar values are estimates, not exact WGI. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

Slovakia.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 high but with Mecir-era political dysfunction -> MI slightly lower than Czech, slightly wider spread; still well above Yugoslav/post-Soviet floors. WGI Rule of Law high (slightly below Czech); Govt Effectiveness moderate-high; Regulatory Quality high but Mecir-era backsliding. HDI 1995 high band (similar to Czech); GDP per cap PPP 1996 ~20% lower; political stability high but illiberal drift under Mecir. Triggers Safeguard F (sub-state/political turbulence in a high-P1 state). Pillar values are estimates, not exact WGI. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Czech Republic better trajectory (higher P1), but both succeed.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Czech P1 >= Slovakia P1, both well above the bottom-third Rule-of-Law gate.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Slovakia clearly out-trajectories the Czech Republic, or either fails outright.

b_violence.prediction: Peaceful -- high P1 predicts a negotiated outcome. Explicit contrast with Yugoslavia: same era, same event type (federation dissolution), but Czechoslovakia's far higher P1 -> 'Velvet Divorce' with zero deaths vs Yugoslavia's 130,000-140,000 war dead.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: The dissolution produces inter-state or ethnic violence.

c_convergence.prediction: Convergence (both converge upward to EU core).
c_convergence.basis: Both high P1; both above the gate.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Persistent divergence between the two successors.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Primary success dimension is P1/institutions for both.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Success/failure driven by a non-P1 dimension.

e_fragment_count.prediction: 2 successors = natural/manageable range, gated by high P1 -> manageable peaceful fragmentation.
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: Low fragment count plus high P1 still yields an unmanageable/violent breakup.

h_substate_turbulence.prediction: Slovakia's 1990s Mecir illiberalism = a high-P1 state surviving with political dysfunction (later corrected before 2004 EU accession).
h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Slovakia's turbulence collapses the state rather than being absorbed/corrected.

time_points: qualitative trajectory (not in user M-score dataset)

Czech Republic.outcome_summary: EU 2004; high-income, high-HDI; retained a modest lead. CPI 2024 = 56. Retains the koruna.

Slovakia.outcome_summary: EU 2004; adopted the euro in 2009 (ahead of Czechia); caught up economically; later governance wobbles (CPI 2024 = 49, somewhat lower than Czechia, consistent with the slightly lower 1996 P1). Mecir-era illiberalism corrected before 2004 accession.
key_events: correction of Mecir-era illiberalism before EU accession

result_coding_reference.CONFIRMED: Prediction matched outcome on the specific dimension predicted
result_coding_reference.PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: Direction correct but magnitude, form, or timing significantly different
result_coding_reference.NOT_APPLICABLE: Prediction type not relevant to this case
result_coding_reference.coding_rule: When ambiguous between confirmed and partial, code PARTIAL. When ambiguous between partial and falsified, code PARTIAL but note ambiguity.

analysis.overall_assessment: The framework's flagship result and single cleanest validation. Holding event type constant (multinational federation dissolution, same years, same end-of-communism trigger), the only major difference is institutional quality, and outcomes split exactly as P1 predicts: high P1 -> bloodless divorce; lower P1 (Yugoslavia) -> war. All applicable predictions CONFIRMED.
safeguards_triggered: B (2 successors, natural/manageable range gated by high P1)
F (Slovakia Mecir-era sub-state turbulence in a high-P1 state)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: As close to a controlled natural experiment as the validation set offers. Scholars note the puzzle that Czechoslovakia's two societies were more alike at dissolution than at founding, making institutional quality and elite strategy -- not ethnic difference -- the operative variable, aligning precisely with the MI's complexity-capacity-matching logic.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; strengthens the P1-predicts-violence-vs-peace claim. No baseline-breaking modification proposed.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; narrow-gap a-trajectory annotated with Mod4). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
